sources.name: Epidemiology of accelerometer-based sleep parameters in US school-aged children and adults: NHANES 2011-2014 (Sleep Health, 2022, PMC9090869)
sources.measures: Device-measured nightly sleep duration: duration of the sleep period time window (longest sleep block in each noon-to-noon day) minus summed wake bouts, from an ActiGraph GT3X+ worn on the wrist for 7 days; participants needed at least 3 valid days; nights under 3 h or over 15 h excluded. NHANES 2011-2012 and 2013-2014 cycles, 4-year survey weights.
sources.notes: No all-adult median is published; Table 2 gives percentiles per adult age band only. The values above are the 46-55 band (n=1313), chosen because NHANES adult mean age is about 48. Full table, 5th/10th/25th/50th/75th/90th in hours: 18-25 (n=1047) 6.53/6.98/7.50/8.22/8.97/9.51; 26-35 (n=1148) 6.43/6.78/7.37/8.01/8.78/9.42; 36-45 (n=1277) 6.27/6.65/7.28/7.90/8.54/9.32; 46-55 (n=1313) 6.21/6.54/7.18/7.83/8.62/9.41; 56-65 (n=1385) 5.98/6.52/7.19/7.91/8.71/9.51; 66-75 (n=1011) 6.38/6.79/7.44/8.24/9.14/9.94; 76+ (n=742) 6.46/6.80/7.53/8.26/9.10/9.85. Adult medians therefore span 7.83 to 8.26 h. Whole-sample mean including children aged 6+ is 8.19 h (SE 0.02). n is the sum of the adult bands (7,923); total sample 11,279. Accelerometer sleep period time tends to run longer than polysomnography-measured sleep.

sources.name: Tracking the night: measuring age and sex patterns in sleep duration using wearable technology (Sleep, 2026)
sources.measures: Longest continuous nighttime sleep period between 6 pm and 6 am as recorded by a Samsung Galaxy Watch, averaged per person over February to April 2023; US adults aged 20-69 with at least 20 valid weekdays and 8 valid weekend days.
sources.notes: Median not reported in the available abstract text. Overall mean 7.57 h (7 h 34 min); 10th to 90th percentile 6.5 to 8.9 h; 23.0% sleep under 7 h. SD reported by sex only: women 1.61 h, men 1.54 h; women sleep 18 min more than men on average. Age-band means: 40-49 shortest at 7.54 h, 60-69 longest at 7.75 h. Sample is gated on owning and wearing a Samsung watch, so not population-representative.

definition: Device-measured nightly sleep duration: duration of the sleep period time window (longest sleep block in each noon-to-noon day) minus summed wake bouts, from an ActiGraph GT3X+ worn on the wrist for 7 days; participants needed at least 3 valid days; nights under 3 h or over 15 h excluded. NHANES 2011-2012 and 2013-2014 cycles, 4-year survey weights.
caveat: No source publishes a single median for all adults. The only published medians are device-measured NHANES values by adult age band (7.83 to 8.26 h, 2011-2014); the 46-55 band is shown as representative. Wearable and under-mattress datasets (Samsung, Withings) give means around 7.1 to 7.6 h and are gated on owning the device. Self-reported means are 7.0 to 7.6 h on workdays, and the BLS time-diary average of 9.03 h counts time in bed, naps and wakefulness, so it is not comparable. The question names no country; US data were used because they are the only ones with published percentiles, while the world-level source gives a mean and SD only. All sources are independent of one another.

new_metric.label: Nightly sleep duration
new_metric.definition: Hours of sleep obtained in a typical night, measured by a wrist accelerometer over at least three nights (self-reported figures run longer).
